paper.title: TopRank: A practical algorithm for online stochastic ranking

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning to rank in a generalized stochastic click model
unmapped: Click probability v(a,k) of each position depends on the whole ranking a; it need not factor into attractiveness times examination

Generalized click model defined by Assumptions 1-4 (no clicks beyond position K, sorting by attractiveness is optimal, pairwise-exchange inequality v(a,a^{-1}(i)) >= alpha(i)/alpha(j) v(sigma∘a, a^{-1}(i)), positions are examined least under the optimal ranking); includes cascade, position-based and document-based models
Clicks on different items may be dependent; multiple clicks are allowed
L items, K displayed slots (paper's K is the list length m)
settings.definition_quote: In each round $t$ the learner chooses an action $A_t \in \cA$ based on its observations so far and observes binary random variables $C_{t1}, \ldots, C_{tL}$ where $C_{ti} = 1$ if the user clicked on item $i$. ... $\bbP(C_{tA_t(k)} = 1 \mid A_t = a) = v(a, k)$

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning to rank in a generalized stochastic click model (lower bound)
unmapped: Generalized click model defined by Assumptions 1-4; the hard instances are document-based models (equivalently m-set semi-bandits)
L items, K displayed slots (paper's K is the list length m)
settings.definition_quote: Suppose that $L = NK$ with $N$ an integer and $n \ge K$ and $n \geq N$ and $N \ge 8$. Then for any algorithm there exists a ranking problem such that $\EE[R_n] \geq \sqrt{K L n} / (16 \sqrt{2})$.

symbols.sum_pairs: sum over items j in [L] and i in [min(K, j-1)] of its argument

conditions: alpha(1) > alpha(2) > ... > alpha(L) (distinct attractiveness, used only to simplify the expression)

source.label: thm:ranking:main
source.quote: Let function $v$ satisfy Assumptions~\ref{ass:zero}--\ref{ass:lowest-exam} and $\alpha(1) > \alpha(2) > \cdots > \alpha(L)$. Let $\Delta_{ij} = \alpha(i) - \alpha(j)$ and $\delta \in (0, 1)$. Then the $n$-step regret of $\toprank$ is bounded from above as R_n \leq \delta n K L^2 + \sum_{j=1}^L \sum_{i=1}^{\min\{K, j-1\}} (1 + 6(\alpha(i) + \alpha(j))\log(c \sqrt{n}/\delta)/\Delta_{ij}).

results.notes: Regret defined via click probabilities v, i.e. pseudo-regret. Algorithm does not use n, but the paper recommends delta = 1/n giving O(sum_j sum_{i<=min(K,j-1)} alpha(i) log(n)/Delta_ij). Paper's K mapped to m, items L declared.

bound.expression_latex: R_n \leq \delta n K L^2 + KL + \sqrt{4K^3 L n \log\left(\frac{c\sqrt{n}}{\delta}\right)}

source.label: thm:ranking:main
source.quote: Furthermore, $\displaystyle R_n \leq \delta n K L^2 + KL + \sqrt{4K^3 L n \log\left(\frac{c\sqrt{n}}{\delta}\right)}$\,.

results.notes: With delta = 1/n gives O(sqrt(K^3 L n log n)) as stated in text.

bound.regime: L = N K with N integer, n >= K, n >= N, N >= 8

symbols.N_blk: L/K, integer number of items per block

conditions: L = N K with N an integer
hard instances are document-based click models with conditionally independent clicks

source.label: thm:minimax lower bound
source.quote: Suppose that $L = NK$ with $N$ an integer and $n \ge K$ and $n \geq N$ and $N \ge 8$. Then for any algorithm there exists a ranking problem such that $\EE[R_n] \geq \sqrt{K L n} / (16 \sqrt{2})$.

results.notes: Also stated to give a lower bound for m-sets in semi-bandit combinatorial linear optimization.
